'''Ents''' are [[monsters]] found in the [[ent cavern]] beneath the [[Woodcutting Guild]] and in the forests north and east of the [[Chaos Temple (Wilderness)|Chaos Temple]]. Ents are found on [[members]]' worlds exclusively.

Upon death, the ent's trunk will fall and remain on the ground for 1 minute. These remains can be chopped to give several sets of [[noted]] [[logs]] according to the player's [[Woodcutting]] level. Players also have a chance to receive a [[bird nest]] while chopping the ent trunk. While cutting the trunk, players get 25 [[experience]] per set of logs received no matter the type. Completing the [[medium Wilderness Diary]] increases the chance of successfully chopping ents in the Wilderness by 15%.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1061345040105172993|date=10 November 2018|archiveurl=https://reldo.runescape.wiki/i/102365|archivedate=28 May 2020|quote=Around 15% higher chance of a "successful" roll when chopping.}} Ents can be safespotted by moving 1-3 tiles adjacent to a tree and using a ranged weapon, halberd, or magic attack.

Chopping the trunks requires an [[axe]] that the player has the Woodcutting level to use. The type of logs that can be received is determined by a player's base Woodcutting level, with higher levels giving better logs. The chance to successfully receive logs is determined by the player's current Woodcutting level (boosted or drained), with higher levels increasing success chance. The distribution of log types is determined by the axe used, with better axes providing a greater amount of higher tier logs. 

While Ents do drop [[slayer's enchantment]]s, while on a Wilderness slayer task, they do not drop [[looting bag]]s or [[Larran's key]]s.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1262839307456438274|date=19 May 2020|archiveurl=https://reldo.runescape.wiki/i/100973|archivedate=20 June 2020}} Unlike logs which are chopped from the trunk, slayer's enchantments are dropped when the ent is killed.

Ent trunks are only choppable by the player who originally killed the ent. When an ent dies its trunk lasts for 101 [[ticks]] (60.6 seconds), so chopping it as soon as it appears gives 25 chances to receive logs. In the Wilderness, the ent respawns 15 ticks after the log despawns, for a total of 116 ticks from death to respawn. In the Woodcutting Guild, this takes 50 ticks, for a total of 151 from death to respawn.

{{External|rs=Implings}} [[File:Eclectic impling.png|120px|right]] '''Implings''' are [[Hunter]] creatures that are featured in the [[minigame]] [[Impetuous Impulses]]. They are mainly found in [[Puro-Puro]], but they can be found commonly across [[Gielinor]]. Higher level requirement implings typically have more valuable loot. Players must wield a [[butterfly net]] or [[magic butterfly net]] to be able to '''catch''' implings, but doing so with an empty [[impling jar]] in their inventory allows players to keep them (either to open later or sell at the [[Grand Exchange]]). Players can also catch implings barehanded, but this requires 10 Hunter levels above the requirement for catching that impling (for example, [[ninja impling]]s barehanded requires level 84 Hunter instead of the normal 74). Implings caught without an impling jar will be looted immediately. An impling jar is '''required''' to catch implings in '''Puro'''-'''Puro'''. However, if you have a jar in your inventory, you can barehand the impling into the jar. Grabbing an impling with your bare hands has the same success rate as attempting to catch one with a magic butterfly net.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1413192817275457546|date=8 July 2021|archiveurl=https://reldo.runescape.wiki/i/104105|archivedate=21 May 2022|quote=The raw chances are 12% at level 1 (if that were allowed) and 98% at level 99; interpolate linearly between those. For barehanded or a magic net, add 8 percentage points to the chances - which means you do get a no-fail chance.}} Three empty impling jars can be acquired from [[Elnock Inquisitor]] in Puro-Puro for any type of jarred impling. This can be a good use for young and baby implings, given their low value loot. They can also be generated with a [[jar generator]] (33 jars from a generator, one at a time). Implings have the ability to fly over any body of water or lava, but not over obstacles that can be labelled with a line on the [[minimap]]. They can occasionally teleport to a nearby area which can cause complications when inside some thick walls, for example the wall east of [[Taverley]]. This can make them impossible to catch and can only be fixed if the impling either teleports out or despawns. A [[wandering impling]] roams around the large wheat field in [[Zanaris]]. He cannot be caught, but he introduces players to the [[Impetuous Impulses]] minigame in an eccentric manner and will show players the location of the two other portals outside of Puro-Puro. Another visually identical impling, [[Immenizz]], can be found near the centre of Puro-Puro. He will explain briefly why implings might be hiding what humans may want. [[Fairy Aeryka]] is found near the wandering impling, and she will also give her version of what implings are, and what is in Puro-Puro. Unlike most other hunter creatures, players can use the spells [[Bind]], [[Snare]], and [[Entangle]] to keep an impling from moving further away, as well as [[Dark Lure]] to force them to approach the player. This can be useful when in Puro-Puro, or to keep an impling from flying over a body of water. After tagging an impling successfully with a Binding spell, players have a few seconds of grace during which other players cannot attempt to catch the tagged impling. ==Types of implings== {{otheruses|def=no|a table of implings as a source of clue scrolls|Treasure Trails/Strategies#Opening impling jars}} {| class="wikitable sortable align-center-1 align-center-3 align-center-4 align-center-5" ! rowspan=2 colspan=2 |Name ! rowspan=2 |{{SCP|Hunter}} level

The expected value is much higher if, for example, using the shards to make divine potions.}} |- |[[File:Dragon impling.png|x55px]] |[[Dragon impling]] |83 (93) |65 |300 |{{Coins|{{GEP|Dragon impling jar}}}} |{{Coins|{{ImpValue|Dragon}}}} |- |[[File:Lucky impling.png|x55px]] |[[Lucky impling]] |89 (99) |80 |380 |{{NA}} |{{Coins|{{ImpValue|Lucky}}}} |} {{Reflist|group="d"}} {{Notelist}} ==Tracker== [[File:Surface world impling tracker.png|thumb|Surface world impling tracker]] [[File:Puro-Puro impling tracker.png|thumb|Puro-Puro impling tracker]] Players can right-click their [[butterfly net]] or [[magic butterfly net]] to open the impling tracker interface, which tracks how many implings they have caught inside Puro-Puro and on the surface world. It contains two tabs, one for implings caught on the surface world, and one for implings caught in [[Puro-Puro]]. Implings that are caught barehanded are also tracked on this log. The tracker will still work without a butterfly net in the player's inventory or bank. ==Money making== {{Mmgsection|Hunting implings}} ==Spawn mechanics== {{Listen |title=A wild gourmet impling appeared! |image=[[File:Impling appears.gif]] |filename=Impling_spawn.ogg |align=right }} Implings have a variety of methods in which they spawn. In most cases, they initially spawn as an invisible NPC, and "roam" invisibly for two minutes,{{fact|Unsure if 2 minutes exactly or between 1-3 minutes.}} during which they can move a considerable distance from their spawn point; implings can even roam over obstacles, such as bodies of water and [[magical wheat]], a unique ability among NPCs. Once implings become visible, a high-pitched "beckon whistle" sound plays with a subtle rattling. They will roam for approximately thirty minutes before disappearing. Implings will stay within a radius of a hundred tiles from their spawn point.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1163112315656556544|date=18 August 2019|archiveurl=https://reldo.runescape.wiki/i/27963266|archivedate=7 April 2026|quote=[Thank you for the response. Just a follow up question, do higher tier impling have a set distance they can travel from their original spawn? For example, if a lucky impling spawns in Frankenstein's castle, it can only travel a 100 squares from that spawn.] Yeah, 100 seems fairly common for them.}} When an impling is captured, the invisible NPC will respawn immediately and once again roam for two minutes before becoming visible and determining the type of impling to spawn. If an impling is trapped between a player and scenery such that it can't move, after five minutes it teleports back to its spawn location but remains visible. ===Types of spawn=== There are four types of invisible spawns for implings: low-tier, mid-tier, high-tier, and another high-tier exclusive to [[Puro-Puro]]. These tiers determine the chances for certain types of implings to appear in place of the invisible NPC: ====Low-tier==== {| class="wikitable" !colspan=2 |Impling !Chance |- |{{plinkt|Baby impling|pic=Baby impling jar}} |20/100 |- |{{plinkt|Young impling|pic=Young impling jar}} |20/100 |- |{{plinkt|Gourmet impling|pic=Gourmet impling jar}} |20/100 |- |{{plinkt|Earth impling|pic=Earth impling jar}} |20/100 |- |{{plinkt|Essence impling|pic=Essence impling jar}} |10/100 |- |{{plinkt|Eclectic impling|pic=Eclectic impling jar}} |10/100 |} ====Mid-tier==== {| class="wikitable" !colspan=2 |Impling !Chance |- |{{plinkt|Gourmet impling|pic=Gourmet impling jar}} |10/100 |- |{{plinkt|Earth impling|pic=Earth impling jar}} |10/100 |- |{{plinkt|Essence impling|pic=Essence impling jar}} |20/100 |- |{{plinkt|Eclectic impling|pic=Eclectic impling jar}} |37/100 |- |{{plinkt|Nature impling|pic=Nature impling jar}} |20/100 |- |{{plinkt|Magpie impling|pic=Magpie impling jar}} |2/100 |- |{{plinkt|Ninja impling|pic=Ninja impling jar}} |1/100 |} ====High-tier==== {| class="wikitable" !colspan=2 |Impling !Chance |- |{{plinkt|Nature impling|pic=Nature impling jar}} |10/101 |- |{{plinkt|Magpie impling|pic=Magpie impling jar}} |50/101 |- |{{plinkt|Ninja impling|pic=Ninja impling jar}} |30/101 |- |{{plinkt|Dragon impling|pic=Dragon impling jar}} |10/101 |- |{{plinkt|Lucky impling|pic=Lucky impling jar}} |1/101 |} ====High-tier (Puro-Puro)==== {| class="wikitable" !colspan=2 |Impling !Chance |- |{{plinkt|Nature impling|pic=Nature impling jar}} |150/301 |- |{{plinkt|Magpie impling|pic=Magpie impling jar}} |114/301 |- |{{plinkt|Ninja impling|pic=Ninja impling jar}} |27/301 |- |{{plinkt|Dragon impling|pic=Dragon impling jar}} |9/301 |- |{{plinkt|Lucky impling|pic=Lucky impling jar}} |1/301 |} ===Gielinor=== On Gielinor (the overworld), there are dozens of spawn points. The majority will spawn all types of implings; this occurs every thirty minutes from when the [[server]] boots up (usually Wednesday, ~11:30 UTC). This spawn timer is based on server [[ticks]] rather than time in real life, so the exact timing is not perfectly consistent. Each thirty-minute cycle, any currently wandering implings will despawn. The game will then first roll to determine which invisible NPCs will spawn, and then pick a random spawn location from the points listed in the map below to determine where to place them. After two minutes, the invisible NPCs will become visible implings. This process happens in a few distinct steps: # First, four implings are picked from the high-tier overworld spawn table. # A random number N is then generated with a value of between 5 and 10. # Next, the mid-tier spawn table is rolled N times. # Finally, the game will roll the low-tier spawn table a total of N*2 times. # After each impling is picked, it is assigned to a random spawn point, where it will appear after two minutes. Therefore, there is theoretically no upper limit to how many implings can spawn in a given spawn location, but the chances become exponentially more unlikely as the total number increases. As a result, any more than four implings per spawn is only very rarely observed. Another 10 spawn points on the overworld, plus one within the [[Zanaris]] marketplace, will always spawn an impling from the low-tier table. {{Map|group=invisible_overworld_rollers|zoom=-2|mapID=0|mtype=pin|icon=greenPin|width=762|height=540|align=center|caption=A complete map of impling spawn points on Gielinor.

The invisible NPC will always produce a [[crystal impling]]. {{Map|group=prif|mapID=29|mtype=pin|width=400|height=400|align=center|caption=Crystal impling spawns in Prifddinas.|x=3263|y=6070|3290,6117|3307,6041|3210,6110|3213,6049|3237,6102|3308,6117|3240,6046|3214,6113|3290,6049|3234,6072|3240,6120|3234,6129}} ===Puro-Puro=== On [[Puro-Puro]] (the realm where the [[Impetuous Impulses]] minigame takes place), there are 35 spawn points that produce an invisible NPC which roams for two minutes before manifesting, and respawns immediately upon capture. Of these 35 spawn points, there are 21 low-tier spawns, 12 mid-tier spawns, and 2 high-tier spawns: {{Map|group=invisible_puro_puro|zoom=2|mapID=-1|mtype=pin|width=400|align=center|caption=A map of spawn points in Puro-Puro. Green pins indicate low-tier spawns, yellow indicates mid-tier, and red indicates high-tier. |2576,4336,icon:redPin|2610,4301,icon:redPin |2569,4342,icon:yellowPin|2591,4339,icon:yellowPin|2616,4343,icon:yellowPin|2578,4334,icon:yellowPin|2605,4334,icon:yellowPin|2572,4321,icon:yellowPin|2610,4320,icon:yellowPin|2575,4306,icon:yellowPin|2591,4301,icon:yellowPin|2605,4306,icon:yellowPin|2570,4297,icon:yellowPin|2617,4295,icon:yellowPin |2570,4332,icon:greenPin|2585,4340,icon:greenPin|2603,4340,icon:greenPin|2615,4333,icon:greenPin|2574,4322,icon:greenPin|2609,4322,icon:greenPin|2578,4299,icon:greenPin|2589,4299,icon:greenPin|2598,4302,icon:greenPin|2614,4308,icon:greenPin }} In addition, there are 51 fixed spawns of specific low-tier implings found throughout Puro-Puro. These spawn directly as implings rather than first spending a brief time invisible, and have a set respawn time of 50 ticks (30 seconds) for the earth and essence implings, and of 7 ticks (4.2 seconds) for all other varieties: {{Map|group=static_puro_puro|zoom=3|mapID=-1|mtype=pin|height=600|width=600|align=center|caption=A map of fixed spawn points in Puro-Puro:
{{Legend|#ee4231|caption=[[Baby impling]]}} {{Legend|#6bc71f|caption=[[Young impling]]}} {{Legend|#3ea6e6|caption=[[Gourmet impling]]}} {{Legend|#e874cf|caption=[[Earth impling]]}} {{Legend|#f9d000|caption=[[Essence impling]]}} {{Legend|#949eaa|caption=[[Eclectic impling]]}} |2563,4291,icon:redPin|2563,4348,icon:redPin|2568,4323,icon:redPin|2571,4305,icon:redPin|2571,4337,icon:redPin|2581,4300,icon:redPin|2584,4344,icon:redPin|2596,4296,icon:redPin|2609,4339,icon:redPin|2610,4304,icon:redPin|2615,4322,icon:redPin|2620,4291,icon:redPin|2620,4348,icon:redPin |2564,4321,icon:greenPin|2574,4321,icon:greenPin|2574,4331,icon:greenPin|2587,4300,icon:greenPin|2590,4348,icon:greenPin|2592,4291,icon:greenPin|2595,4343,icon:greenPin|2612,4309,icon:greenPin|2612,4327,icon:greenPin|2619,4322,icon:greenPin |2568,4296,icon:bluePin|2568,4327,icon:bluePin|2574,4311,icon:bluePin|2580,4343,icon:bluePin|2585,4296,icon:bluePin|2597,4293,icon:bluePin|2602,4346,icon:bluePin|2609,4317,icon:bluePin|2615,4298,icon:bluePin|2615,4342,icon:bluePin|2618,4321,icon:bluePin |2568,4317,icon:magentaPin|2570,4330,icon:magentaPin|2574,4305,icon:magentaPin|2587,4342,icon:magentaPin|2590,4298,icon:magentaPin|2598,4340,icon:magentaPin|2611,4334,icon:magentaPin|2612,4310,icon:magentaPin |2574,4317,icon:yellowPin|2576,4337,icon:yellowPin|2585,4298,icon:yellowPin|2601,4343,icon:yellowPin|2612,4318,icon:yellowPin |2567,4319,icon:greyPin|2591,4295,icon:greyPin|2591,4340,icon:greyPin|2615,4326,icon:greyPin }} ===Force-spawning=== The best method to find the rarest and most valuable implings is to force-spawn them. In Puro-Puro, higher tier implings ([[nature impling]]s and above) can be found much more commonly than on Gielinor. This is because, as seen above, Puro-Puro has two specific points which only spawn high-tier implings. As an example, to maximise the amount of [[dragon impling]]s spawning, a player will want to catch all rare implings ([[Nature impling|nature]], [[magpie impling|magpie]], [[ninja impling|ninja]]) as these will have spawned from the higher tier spawn tiles, giving them a chance for a dragon impling to spawn. This is best done at either the north-west or south-east corners of Puro-Puro, and it is advised to hop between multiple worlds because of the 2 minute "respawn"-timer for these higher tier implings. ==Changes== {{Subject changes header}} {{Subject changes |date = 12 January 2022 |update = Nex Changes & Tweaks |change = After tagging an impling successfully with a Binding spell, you now have a few seconds of grace during which other players cannot attempt to catch 'your' impling. }} {{Subject changes |date = 25 July 2019 |update = Song of the Elves |poll = Old School Content Poll 64: Song of the Elves |change = Crystal implings were introduced with the quest, Song of the Elves. }} {{Subject changes |date = 11 April 2019 |update = Treasure Trails Expansion and Easter 2019 |poll = Old School Content Poll 65: Treasure Trails Expansion |change = Beginner clue scrolls have been added to the drop tables of baby and young implings. }} {{Subject changes |date = 16 June 2016 |update = Skotizo - The Archaic Demon |change = Corrected the grammar in game messages when catching implings with your bare hands. }} {{Subject changes |date = 21 April 2016 |update = Deadman Changes & Implings |poll = Old School Content Poll 41: Bank placeholders & Skillcapes |change = * It is now possible to catch implings without a net or jar. * Clue scrolls have been added to the drop tables of implings. }} {{Subject changes |date = 17 March 2016 |update = The Easter Bunny's Workshop |change = A spawn for implings in central Kourend has been moved out of the blocked area. }} {{Subject changes |date = 4 April 2013 |update = Patch Notes (4 April 2013) |change = Hunter implings can now only be caught by one person at a time. }} {{Subject changes footer}} ==References== {{reflist}} {{Impling}} {{Hunter creatures}} {{Demons}} [[Category:Hunter]]

title: Module:Ent calculator
wikitext:
local chart = require( 'Module:Chart data' )

local p = {}

-- Cursed ass table, there's probably a better way to do this but whatever
local dataTable = {
    woodcuttingLevel = { {0, 15}, {16, 30}, {31, 45}, {46, 60}, {61, 74}, {75, 99} },
    woodcuttingAxeOffset = { 
        {0, 10},
        {11, 20},
        {21, 35},
        {36, 50},
        {51, 75},
        {76, 170}
    },
    data = {
        {"Nothing", "Nothing", "Nothing", "Nothing", "Nothing", "Nothing"},
        {"Plain",   "Plain",   "Plain",   "Oak",     "Oak",     "Oak"},
        {"Plain",   "Plain",   "Oak",     "Oak",     "Oak",     "Willow"},
        {"Plain",   "Plain",   "Oak",     "Oak",     "Willow",  "Maple"},
        {"Plain",   "Plain",   "Oak",     "Willow",  "Maple",   "Yew"},
        {"Plain",   "Oak",     "Willow",  "Maple",   "Yew",     "Magic"}
    }
}

local axeOffsets = {
    Bronze = 1,
    Iron = 1,
    Steel = 6,
    Black = 11,
    Mithril = 21,
    Adamant = 31,
    Rune = 41,
    Dragon = 61,
    Crystal = 71
}

local woodTypes = {
    ["Logs"] = "Plain",
    ["Oak logs"] = "Oak",
    ["Willow logs"] = "Willow",
    ["Maple logs"] = "Maple",
    ["Yew logs"] = "Yew",
    ["Magic logs"] = "Magic"
}

local diaryValues = {
    ["true"] = {22, 102},
    ["false"] = {16, 90}
}

-- interp, replace with skill success chart require at some point
local function interp(low, high, level)
    local value = math.floor(low * (99 - level) / 98 + high * (level - 1) / 98 + 0.5) + 1
    return math.min(math.max(value / 256, 0), 1)
end

-- Find the drop table entry
local function getDroptable(value, ranges)
    for i, range in ipairs(ranges) do
        if value >= range[1] and value <= range[2] then
            return i
        end
    end
    return nil
end

-- Calculate cumulative chance for each log type
local function calculateChancesForLogTypes(axeType, axeOffsets, diary)
    local results = {}
    local low, high = unpack(diaryValues[diary])
    local axeOffset = axeOffsets[axeType]
    for woodName, woodType in pairs(woodTypes) do
        local woodChances = {}
        for level = 1, 99 do
            local levelBinIndex = getDroptable(level, dataTable.woodcuttingLevel)
            local rollChance = interp(low, high, level)
            local maxRoll = level + axeOffset
            local chance = 0
            for roll = 1, #dataTable.woodcuttingAxeOffset do
                local item = dataTable.data[roll][levelBinIndex]
                if item == woodType then
                    -- Calculate probability
                    local rangeY = dataTable.woodcuttingAxeOffset[roll]
                    local cap = math.min(rangeY[2], maxRoll)
                    if cap > rangeY[1] then
                        local rangeSize = cap - rangeY[1] + 1
                        chance = chance + ((rangeSize / (maxRoll + 1)))
                    end
                end
            end
            if level >= axeOffset then
                woodChances[level] = (chance * rollChance)
            end
        end
        results[woodName] = woodChances
    end
    return results
end

function p._calculateDataSets(args)
    local logColors = {
        ["Logs"] = "dimgrey",
        ["Oak logs"] = "green",
        ["Willow logs"] = "slateblue",
        ["Maple logs"] = "darkgoldenrod",
        ["Yew logs"] = "brown",
        ["Magic logs"] = "teal"
    }

    local dataSets = {}
    local axeType = args.axeType or "Dragon"
    local diary = args.diary or "true"
    
    local results = calculateChancesForLogTypes(axeType, axeOffsets, diary)
    local axeOffset = axeOffsets[axeType]
    for logType, chances in pairs(results) do
        local data = {}
        for level = axeOffset, 99 do
            table.insert(data, {
                x = level,
                y = chances[level]
            })
        end

		table.insert(dataSets, {
			data = {},
			label = logType,
			borderDash = {5, 5},
			borderCapStyle = 'round',
			pointRadius = 0,
			baseColor = logColors[logType],
			pointStyleImg = logType .. '.png'
	    })
		table.insert(dataSets, {
            data = data,
            label = logType,
            borderDash = {},
            borderCapStyle = 'round',
            pointRadius = 0,
            baseColor = logColors[logType],
        })
        table.insert(dataSets, {})
    end

    return dataSets
end


function p.main(frame)
    local args = frame.args
    return p._main(args)
end

function p._main(args)
	local axeType = args.axeType
    local plot = chart.newChart{ type = 'scatter' }
        :setTitle(args.title or 'Ent Log Chances (' .. axeType .. ' axe)')
        :setDimensions('540px', '400px', '540px', '400px', true)
        :setXLabel(args.xlabel or 'Woodcutting Level')
        :setYLabel(args.ylabel or 'Success Rate (%)')
        :setXLimits(nil, nil, 1)
		:setYLimits(nil, nil, 0.1)
		:setYFormat('percent')
        :setTooltipFormat('skillingSuccess')
        :setDatasetsPerGroup(3)
    
    local dataSets = p._calculateDataSets(args)
    for i, dataSet in ipairs(dataSets) do
        plot:newDataSet(dataSet)
    end

    return plot
end

return p
